outcome: No result addressing the general question of which finite sets C admit a countable universal C-free graph under strong (induced) embeddings was found in the window; the closest 2023-2025 work (Krill, universal graphs with forbidden wheel minors) uses a different containment notion (minors, not induced subgraphs) and was submitted before the window opened.
summary: The bullet is Cherlin's universality problem for C-free countable graphs under strong (induced) embeddings: for which finite sets C of forbidden connected graphs does the class of countable C-free graphs have a universal member under strong embeddings? This traces to Cherlin's long-running program (with Shelah, Komjath, Tallgren, Shi and others), organized around the Solidity Conjecture (if C has an incomplete block, no universal C-free graph exists) and related conjectures about tree/path/near-path cases, most recently advanced in Cherlin-Shelah's 'Block path solidity' (Combinatorica 2016). I found no paper in the 26 Jan 2024 - present window that resolves, extends, or meaningfully moves this general question or the Solidity Conjecture itself. Cherlin's own Rutgers publications page (sites.math.rutgers.edu/~cherlin/Paper/) lists nothing on universal graphs since 2016; his 2024-2025 papers are on unrelated model-theoretic topics (algebraicity, separably closed fields). The most relevant candidate found, Thilo Krill's 'Universal graphs with forbidden wheel minors' (arXiv:2309.12473, published in Journal of Graph Theory 2025), proves universality results for classes defined by forbidding a minor (cycles, theta-graphs, wheels) under a different containment notion than the Wikipedia bullet's 'strong embeddings' (which mean induced-subgraph embeddings in this literature); more importantly it was submitted 21 September 2023, before the 26 January 2024 window opens, so even if judged a case of the stated problem it would be open_stale, not a window event. Krill's paper explicitly frames its own open Conjecture 1.2 as distinct from and only 'lending support to' ideas in the Cherlin program, underscoring that it is not a direct advance on the Wikipedia bullet. A June 2025 paper on 'Infinite induced-saturated graphs' (arXiv:2506.08810) addresses a related but different saturation question and does not bear on universal C-free graphs. No arXiv, Google Scholar, or web search turned up any 2024-2026 paper directly addressing the general universality-for-C-free-graphs question or citing new progress on the Solidity/Pathlike conjectures. I therefore agree with the triage's 'none' verdict; no disagreement.
competing_reading: One could argue Krill's wheel-minor paper is close enough in spirit (same universality-for-forbidden-substructure paradigm, explicitly citing and building on Cherlin-Shelah-Tallgren results) to count as adjacent progress worth flagging, and that if it were somehow read as bearing on the subgraph/induced version of the problem it would predate the window regardless (open_stale). But minors and induced subgraphs are different containment relations addressed by different (if related) conjectures in the literature, and Krill's own paper treats them as separate open problems (his Conjecture 1.2 concerns minor-freeness specifically), so I classify it as a related-but-distinct problem rather than a case or resolution of the stated one.
what_would_settle_it: A paper by Cherlin, Komjath, Shelah, or others explicitly proving or disproving a case of the Solidity Conjecture or the general classification for finite C under strong (induced) embeddings, dated after 26 January 2024, would settle whether anything has happened. Checking Cherlin's personal page periodically and monitoring arXiv math.CO/math.LO for 'universal graph' + 'forbidden subgraph'/'C-free' would be the way to catch it.
